answer: Dampened Age Curve. Each identity's influence grows as a knoll over time, starting near zero and rising with verified activity, while the cost to spawn a fresh identity stays fixed. An attacker must wander through many new identities, each paying full cost for near-zero weight. Sybils yield returns only after sustained aging, so a cipher cannot shortcut influence by volume. Per-identity overhead is constant, but aggregate cost scales linearly while effective weight stays flat.
